calibration.key_insight: sum_6 is hard for SINGLE random programs but NOT for EVOLUTIONARY SEARCH

rpa.note: One seed FAILED - RPA actually performed WORSE than random

verdict_detail: Evolutionary search with 500 gens x pop 50 finds sum_6 in 5/5 seeds WITHOUT blocks. The search budget is still too generous. Blocks provide no advantage because evolution already succeeds.

critical_distinction.implication: The task is hard for random generation but NOT for evolutionary search. Evolution accumulates partial solutions through selection.

what_this_means: A SINGLE random program almost never has all 12 correct
But EVOLUTION over 500 generations builds up the solution incrementally
Selection keeps partial solutions, mutation extends them
After ~500 gens, the full 12-op solution emerges
Blocks don't help because evolution already finds it
what_would_actually_demonstrate_block_va: Reduce search budget: 50 gens, pop 10 (evolution fails)
Use sum_10 (20+ ops) with 100 gens (evolution struggles)
Use sum_20 (40+ ops) - evolution likely fails entirely
Tasks where partial solutions have ZERO fitness (no gradient)
honest_assessment: The ACID system keeps finding that the tasks are not hard enough. This is a VALID and IMPORTANT finding. It means the substrate + evolutionary search is more powerful than expected. To truly test whether discovered mechanisms help, we need tasks where evolutionary search ALSO fails.
